page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-240GB-1xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration consists of 24 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU with 192 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance for LLM inference, with prompt processing reaching 9953.26 tokens per second and text generation achieving 525.92 tokens per second on a small 135M model. Memory bandwidth is strong, recording 4156.98 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 251.17 GB/sec for large-block reads. CPU performance is robust, with a PassMark CPU score of 52754.5 and strong results in extended instructions and encryption tests. However, stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests fall within the average range.

This server offers high resource density, combining a massive 192 GB GPU frame buffer with 240 GB of system memory, making it highly efficient for memory-intensive GPU workloads. A key tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the lack of local storage, which requires external storage solutions. The hardware profile is optimized for large language model inference, deep learning, data science, and memory-intensive database operations.
